title: CWS After the LA Fires
subtitle: CWS’s response to the January 2025 fires: evacuation supplies, translated information and a shared registration system at the Wildfire Resource Hub.
excerpt: CWS’s response to the January 2025 fires: evacuation supplies, translated information and a shared registration system at the Wildfire Resource Hub.

content.alt: A CWS relief table with folded blankets and branded supply bags
content.caption: CWS blankets and bags at a wildfire relief station.

content.text: Following the January 2025 fires in Los Angeles County, Church World Service (CWS) and its local branches packed more than 200 evacuation bags for newcomer families. The bags were fireproof and waterproof. Additionally, CWS helped families find temporary housing and access information in their preferred languages.

Having volunteered with CWS after the fires, I noticed a point in its February 4th update: several relief organizations in Pasadena were working out how a family could register with all of them at once.

For six days, the Wildfire Resource Hub provided food, financial aid, counseling, and housing services in one location. CWS translated preparedness material and supplied 5,000 bags containing supplies and information for survivors. This did not include evacuation bags that it assembled for newcomer families.
At the Hub, an identification tag was being introduced for each family. Instead of repeating the story of losing their home at each desk, they would only need to show this tag.

content.alt: People and service tables in a courtyard beneath a Wildfire Resource Hub banner
content.caption: Assistance providers and families gather at the Wildfire Resource Hub.

content.text: CWS and California Voluntary Organizations Active in Disaster asked a local Children's Disaster Services team to work at the Pasadena Hub for a week. Having someone to care for their children allowed parents to speak to a housing specialist or a counselor close by.
For housing questions and longer-term assistance, the Hub referred people to local providers. CWS also worked with the Los Angeles County Long Term Recovery Group.
